intro: Week 8 opens with the Titans trading Jeffery Simmons to Chicago, the Eagles planning without Jalen Hurts and the Chiefs and Broncos set to settle first place in the AFC West. Four teams sit out the early window: the Texans, Giants, Saints and 49ers are on bye, and the Packers and Panthers already played Thursday. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to the Bears for two first-round picks
top.dek: Tennessee gets Chicago's 2027 and 2028 first-round picks plus a 2027 fourth, and sends Simmons and a 2028 fifth to the Bears. The deal came a day after Simmons said he expected to stay. The four-time Pro Bowl tackle misses Tennessee's game at Cincinnati today.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Jalen Hurts has blood clots in his lungs and is done for the year
top.dek: Philadelphia expects Hurts to miss the rest of 2026 and is unlikely to see him before 2027. Tanner McKee takes over the offense, 1-2 as a starter with 812 yards and six touchdowns. The Eagles are 2-5 after Monday night's loss to Dallas and visit Washington tonight.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Javonte Williams runs for a career-high 155 yards against the Eagles
top.dek: Williams carried 25 times at 6.2 yards a pop and closed out the win with a 2-yard touchdown with 2:21 left. He had averaged 49 yards a game over the two games before it. Dallas hosts Arizona today.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 907: Bijan Robinson's scrimmage yards, most in the NFL
top.dek: Robinson has 704 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 5.4 yards per carry through Week 7. He totaled 122 scrimmage yards in last week's upset of San Francisco. Atlanta visits Tampa Bay today at 1 p.m. ET.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Chiefs visit the Broncos at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS with first place on the line
top.dek: Kansas City is 5-1 and leads 5-2 Denver by a half game. A Chiefs win gives them the head-to-head tiebreaker and a two-game cushion in the loss column. Watch the Broncos pass rush against Patrick Mahomes.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills host Ravens with a seeding edge at stake

stories.text: Bills get Lamar Jackson in a game with AFC seeding on the line
stories.summary: Ravens coach Jesse Minter confirmed that quarterback Lamar Jackson will play despite an ankle injury. Buffalo (5-1) carries a two-game winning streak into the matchup, while Baltimore (4-3) has lost two straight. Bolavip noted earlier in the week that the top seed in the AFC earns home-field advantage and the only first-round bye, which gives this game extra weight.

stories.text: Five Bills on the report, with DJ Moore and Dalton Kincaid questionable
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore (shoulder), tight end Dalton Kincaid (chest), tackle Spencer Brown (back), cornerback Dee Alford (ankle) and lineman Greg Gaines are all listed as questionable. Receiver Tyrell Shavers (knee) is out. Baltimore will be without safety Jaylinn Hawkins and guard Vega Ioane.

stories.text: Josh Allen runs the Bills offense with his arm and his legs
stories.summary: Allen has thrown for 1,504 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions through six games. He also has eight rushing touchdowns, the most on the roster. Baltimore has to defend both.

stories.text: 6: Greg Rousseau sacks, most on the Bills
stories.summary: Rousseau leads Buffalo with six sacks and sets the tone up front. Linebacker Dorian Williams leads the team with 46 tackles. Buffalo will lean on that front to pressure Jackson today.

stories.text: Ravens at Highmark Stadium, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo hosts Baltimore in Orchard Park, where the forecast calls for sunny skies, about 54 degrees and a light west wind. Watch whether Moore and Kincaid play and how the Bills pressure Jackson. The game is a potential tiebreaker in the AFC race.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins chase a second win against New England

stories.text: Hafley and the Dolphins look to build on their first win
stories.summary: Jeff Hafley earned his first victory as Miami's coach last Sunday, a 28-25 win over the Jets that kept the Dolphins from an 0-6 start. Malik Willis threw two touchdown passes, ran for a score and finished the game with a fourth-and-1 sneak. Miami (1-5) hosts New England this afternoon.

stories.text: Kadyn Proctor out with a concussion, two corners questionable
stories.summary: Offensive lineman Kadyn Proctor will not play because of a concussion. Cornerbacks JuJu Brents (neck) and Reese Taylor (quad) are questionable, though both practiced fully on Friday. Quarterback Malik Willis (groin) and running back Jaylen Wright (foot and quad) also appeared on the report and have no game designation.

stories.text: Rookie Caleb Douglas scored both times he touched the ball
stories.summary: Douglas caught two passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets. His first score came on Miami's opening drive and gave the team its first lead of the season. His second was a 63-yard catch from Willis that put the Dolphins up 28-17 with 4:44 left.

stories.text: 6: sacks by the Dolphins defense, last in the NFL
stories.summary: Miami has six sacks on the season, and its pressure rate of 35.3 percent ranks 28th. Opponents complete 76.6 percent of their passes against the Dolphins, the worst rate in the league. That is the matchup Drake Maye brings to Hard Rock Stadium today.

stories.text: Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami hosts New England in Miami Gardens. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez leads the NFL with 28 defensive stops, and the Dolphins run defense grades better than their pass defense. Watch whether Miami can create pressure without blitzing much, since its blitz rate is 24.7 percent.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots visit Miami without A.J. Brown

stories.text: Patriots try to reset after a Bears loss ended their win streak
stories.summary: New England lost 30-24 at Chicago on Thursday night, ending a three-game winning streak and dropping to 4-3. The offensive line has been in flux: the Bears game used the team's 10th different line combination, against seven all of last season. Guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Mike Onwenu went on injured reserve this week.

stories.text: A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson are out at Miami
stories.summary: Receiver A.J. Brown (ankle and knee) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) will miss the game. Cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck) and linebacker Christian Elliss (chest) are questionable. Quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) practiced fully and has no designation.

stories.text: Drake Maye has played at a high level for four straight games
stories.summary: Maye has completed 90 of 134 passes for 1,199 yards, 14 total touchdowns and two interceptions over his last four games, for a 119.0 passer rating. He threw for 321 yards against the Bears in his last outing. The Dolphins have the league's worst completion percentage allowed.

stories.text: 70: rushing yards against Chicago, well under the team average
stories.summary: The Patriots ran for just 70 yards in the loss to the Bears, compared with a season average of 130.7 per game. They are also minus-7 in turnover differential through seven games. Those two numbers explain much of the gap in a six-point loss.

stories.text: At Dolphins, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: New England visits Hard Rock Stadium with Brown out and Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on injured reserve. DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III are the healthy receivers, so tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon should see more work. Watch how Maye attacks a Miami secondary that has struggled in coverage.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets host Raiders as Glenn's seat heats up

stories.text: Aaron Glenn's job status hangs over the Jets
stories.summary: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that sources expect Glenn to coach out the season before the team evaluates him, and he calls the hot seat conversation real. The Jets are 2-5 after a 28-25 home loss to Miami. A source also told Fowler the Jets will not trade receiver Garrett Wilson before the deadline.

stories.text: Breece Hall questionable with a quad injury
stories.summary: Glenn listed running back Breece Hall as questionable for the Raiders game because of a quadriceps injury. Defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat hurt his knee against Miami and did not return to that game. Braelon Allen ran for 104 yards in that loss and would carry the load if Hall sits.

stories.text: Geno Smith has been one of the league's most accurate passers
stories.summary: Smith has thrown for 1,623 yards with 10 touchdowns and two interceptions through seven games, completing 70 percent of his passes. Against Miami he went 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three scores. He played for the Raiders last season and led the NFL with 17 interceptions, and now he faces his old team.

stories.text: 8: straight losses to AFC East teams under Aaron Glenn
stories.summary: Miami's 28-25 win last Sunday stretched the Jets' losing streak against division opponents to eight games under Glenn. Geno Smith threw for 287 yards and three touchdowns, and Braelon Allen ran for 104 yards. The Jets trailed 21-7 at halftime and never took the lead.

stories.text: Raiders at MetLife Stadium, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Jets (2-5) host Las Vegas (3-4), which has lost four straight and allows about 374 yards per game. Watch rookie edge David Bailey, who has 5.5 sacks and three forced fumbles, and Smith against his former team. Brock Bowers leads Las Vegas with 455 receiving yards.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Lamar Jackson set to return at Buffalo

stories.text: Jackson expected back at Buffalo after three missed games
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson has not played since halftime of Week 4 because of a high-ankle sprain. Baltimore sits last in the AFC North at 4-3 after back-to-back division losses, and it travels to a Bills team that is 5-1. Reporters on the scene say Jackson is confident he will play, though one report still lists him questionable.

stories.text: Hawkins and Ioane questionable as Jackson's ankle clears
stories.summary: Safety Jaylinn Hawkins and guard Vega Ioane both carry knee designations into Sunday, and one tracker has each ruled out while another has them questionable. Running back Adam Randall (neck) and cornerback T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee) are questionable. Jackson carries no designation in the Yahoo tracker, but the SI preview lists him questionable, so confirm before kickoff.

stories.text: Zay Flowers keeps producing without Jackson
stories.summary: Flowers caught eight passes for 137 yards and a touchdown in last Sunday's 35-13 loss to Cincinnati. Tyler Huntley threw for 298 yards in that game, and Flowers was his top target. Baltimore is 1-2 in Huntley's three starts.

stories.text: 0-for-3: Baltimore's red zone day against Cincinnati
stories.summary: The Ravens failed to score a touchdown on any of three red zone trips in Week 7 and took 10 penalties for 57 yards. They led by 13 at the half and still lost by 22. Cleaner trips inside the 20 are the first fix for Sunday.

stories.text: At Buffalo, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Ravens visit Highmark Stadium to face a Bills team coming off its bye. Buffalo's defense ranks 30th in opponent EPA per play, so the Ravens should find room if Jackson is healthy. Watch his mobility on early designed runs.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals roll into Titans game on top

stories.text: Burrow's four touchdowns bury Baltimore after the bye
stories.summary: Cincinnati trailed 13-0 at halftime in Baltimore and scored 35 straight in the second half. Joe Burrow went 22 of 30 for 292 yards and four touchdowns with no interceptions. The 35-13 win moved the Bengals to 4-2.

stories.text: Dugger out, Chase cleared for Tennessee
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) is out after missing all three practices. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is questionable. Ja'Marr Chase sat out Wednesday with an ankle issue and then practiced fully Thursday and Friday with no designation.

stories.text: Tee Higgins goes for 148 in Baltimore
stories.summary: Higgins caught six passes for 148 yards and a 13-yard touchdown against the Ravens. Chase added five catches for 62 yards and a score. Burrow now has 15 touchdowns and three interceptions on the year.

stories.text: 5-for-5: Bengals finish every red zone trip
stories.summary: Cincinnati scored a touchdown on all five red zone trips against Baltimore and sacked Tyler Huntley four times. The Ravens went 0-for-3 inside the 20. That gap decided the game after halftime.

stories.text: Titans visit Paycor Stadium, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati (4-2) hosts Tennessee (1-6). The Titans will be without rookie receiver Carnell Tate, and running back Tyjae Spears is out. Watch how the Bengals handle Calvin Ridley, who is questionable with a hip issue.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns carry five-game win streak into Pittsburgh

stories.text: Watson wins another one in the fourth quarter
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards, ran in a 9-yard touchdown and led his fifth game-winning drive of the season in a 27-24 win at Tennessee. Andre Szmyt kicked a 32-yard field goal as time expired. Cleveland is 5-2 and has won five of its last six.

stories.text: Howard in concussion protocol, two defenders limited
stories.summary: Right tackle Tytus Howard missed all three practices after a concussion against Tennessee and is questionable. Cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring) and safety Daniel Thomas (ankle) were limited all week and also carry questionable tags. Howard can play only if he clears protocol before kickoff.

stories.text: Rookie KC Concepcion posts a season-best 129 yards
stories.summary: Concepcion caught eight passes for 129 yards in Nashville, his best game this season. Quinshon Judkins added 96 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Cleveland produced 491 total yards against the Titans.

stories.text: 19.0: Browns points per game, 21.9 for Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Cleveland averages 19.0 points and 299.4 yards per game through Week 7, behind Pittsburgh's 21.9 and 323.7. The Steelers also lead in third-down rate, 38.0 percent to 32.6. The Browns have made up the difference with late drives.

stories.text: At Pittsburgh, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Browns and Steelers are both 5-2, with Cleveland holding the tiebreaker from its 27-24 win in Week 4. Pittsburgh is a 3.5-point favorite at DraftKings. Watch whether Watson can solve a defense ranked fifth in points allowed.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers ride three straight wins into Browns game

stories.text: Steelers win in Paris and pull even in the division
stories.summary: Pittsburgh beat New Orleans 16-10 in the NFL's first regular-season game in France for its third straight win. The 5-2 record ties Cleveland atop the AFC North. Aaron Rodgers threw his 540th career touchdown, passing Peyton Manning for third all time.

stories.text: Echols and Slaughter out, Skowronek questionable
stories.summary: Cornerback Brandin Echols and defensive back Doneiko Slaughter are out with hamstring injuries. Receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) is questionable. Safety DeShon Elliott played against the Saints for the first time in a year after his knee injury.

stories.text: Payton Wilson picks off two in Paris
stories.summary: Wilson intercepted Tyler Shough in the red zone and again on the Saints' first drive of the second half, which set up a field goal. Jaylen Warren added 101 rushing yards on 18 carries. Wilson has become a steady piece on a defense that ranks fifth in points allowed.

stories.text: 18: rushing yards the Saints managed on 17 carries
stories.summary: Pittsburgh held New Orleans to 18 yards on the ground in Paris. Saints coach Kellen Moore pointed to that number when explaining the loss. The Steelers now face a Cleveland run defense ranked 22nd in yards per carry allowed.

stories.text: Browns visit Acrisure Stadium, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts Cleveland with first place in the division at stake. The Steelers then go on their Week 9 bye. Rodgers has been sacked nine times in the three games since the Week 4 loss in Cleveland.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans use the bye to fix an 0-4 home mark

stories.text: Texans reach the bye at 2-5 after an overtime loss to the Giants
stories.summary: Houston lost 27-21 to the Giants on Oct. 25 and sits 0-4 at home, with three of those four losses by one score. C.J. Stroud took responsibility and called the bye a chance to self-scout and hold people accountable. The Texans do not play this week, then travel to the Chargers and the Browns.

stories.text: Safeties Pitre and Blankenship sat out the Giants loss
stories.summary: Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship were both out against New York, which thinned the back end of the defense. The Giants ran for 124 yards from Cam Skattebo alone. Receiver Jaylin Noel left in the fourth quarter with turf toe and was seen in a walking boot, and his status is still being evaluated.

stories.text: Tank Dell is back after more than 670 days
stories.summary: Dell played his first game since the knee injury that ended his 2024 season, and coach DeMeco Ryans said the team expects to raise his workload. Stroud heads into the bye with 1,867 passing yards, 11 touchdown passes and one interception. His 17-of-28, 153-yard day against the Giants included the tying 3-yard touchdown throw to Xavier Hutchinson with 57 seconds left.

stories.text: 342: yards per game the Texans defense allows
stories.summary: That is up from 277.2 last season, and it explains much of the 0-4 home start. Houston missed 17 tackles against the Giants, according to PFF, and the offense converted 3 of 12 third downs. The bye gives the staff a week to fix both.

stories.text: Texans are off, then head to Los Angeles to face the Chargers
stories.summary: Houston is on its bye this week with no game Sunday. The next two games are both on the road, first at the Chargers and then at the Browns. Watch whether the penalties (10 for 80 yards against the Giants) and the run defense look cleaner after the break.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts sell Nelson and Buckner, then visit Jacksonville

stories.text: Colts trade Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner
stories.summary: Indianapolis sent guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco this week, with more moves rumored. The team also recently fired general manager Chris Ballard. Daniel Jones said he cannot control questions about his own future and will focus on preparing to play.

stories.text: Walley and Gould out, Boettcher and Ogletree questionable
stories.summary: Slot corner Justin Walley (knee) and receiver Anthony Gould (concussion) are out at Jacksonville. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) are questionable, and Boettcher did not practice all week. Gould is the starting punt returner.

stories.text: Jonathan Taylor draws trade interest with 8 touchdowns
stories.summary: Indianapolis is open to trading Taylor and is talking with teams, per ESPN and NFL Network as relayed by CBS Sports. Five clubs have shown some interest, and at least one offer includes a second-round pick. Taylor, who has eight rushing touchdowns through seven games, said he is proud to play for the Colts and has not asked to be traded.

stories.text: 0: career 100-yard games for Taylor in Jacksonville
stories.summary: When Taylor tops 100 yards against the Jaguars, the Colts are 3-0. When he does not, they are 0-6. He ran for 74 and 70 yards in last year's meetings.

stories.text: Colts visit the Jaguars Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Indianapolis plays at EverBank Stadium against a Jacksonville team coming off its bye. Jacksonville writers say the Colts have not won there since 2014. Watch how the Colts block without Nelson and whether Taylor gets loose on a run defense that struggled against Houston.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars come off the bye to host the Colts

stories.text: Jaguars return from the bye with run defense on the clock
stories.summary: Jacksonville is 4-2 and hosts Indianapolis after a loss to Houston in London, where its run defense had its worst day of the season. Jaguars writers say coach Liam Coen has made stopping explosive plays the post-bye priority. The Jaguars have not allowed a 100-yard rusher since Jonathan Taylor in January 2025.

stories.text: Antonio Johnson out, Jakobi Meyers questionable
stories.summary: Safety Antonio Johnson is out with an ankle injury. Receiver Jakobi Meyers is questionable with hamstring and ankle issues after sitting out Friday's practice, and he said he felt okay. If Meyers cannot go, Brian Thomas Jr. and Josh Cameron would join Parker Washington among the top three receivers.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence has 14 touchdown passes through six games
stories.summary: Analyst Bucky Brooks called Lawrence's play MVP level heading into the bye. Against Houston he beat Ryans' blitzes with quick throws into vacated space. Drops and red-zone misses kept the offense from doing more, Brooks wrote.

stories.text: 0: sacks on 14 pressures against Houston
stories.summary: Per PFF, Jacksonville generated 14 pressures on C.J. Stroud and finished none of them. Josh Hines-Allen had three of the pressures and Travon Walker two. Brooks argues the pass rush has to return for the 4-2 start to hold up.

stories.text: Jaguars host the Colts Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at EverBank Stadium, and rain is forecast for a wet field. Jacksonville is chasing its sixth win in seven meetings, per local writers. Watch Taylor against Foye Oluokun and the Jaguars' ability to stop big plays.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans trade Simmons, then visit the Bengals

stories.text: Titans trade Jeffery Simmons to the Bears
stories.summary: Tennessee sent the four-time Pro Bowl tackle to Chicago for two first-round picks and other draft compensation. Simmons will miss Sunday's game at Cincinnati. The Titans are 1-6, and Cincinnati's Chase said the front still has good players up front.

stories.text: Spears, Tate and Townsend out at Cincinnati
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), rookie receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) are out. Calvin Ridley (hip), John Franklin-Myers (groin/back), Dorian Mausi (foot) and Jaylon Jones (knee) are questionable. Franklin-Myers now leads the defensive line without Simmons.

stories.text: Tony Pollard ran for 129 yards and 3 touchdowns
stories.summary: Pollard carried 25 times against Cleveland in the 27-24 loss and added three catches for 26 yards. He took 25 of the team's 28 running back carries because Spears was inactive. With Spears out again, Pollard should carry the load in Cincinnati.

stories.text: 3: tries from the Cleveland 1 that failed
stories.summary: Tennessee led 14-0 and 14-7 but got stopped on a Cam Ward sneak, a third-down sack and a fourth-down run by Pollard. The Browns tied it and won on the final play. Ward finished 20 of 31 for 181 yards and went 2 of 7 on deep throws.

stories.text: Titans visit the Bengals Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati is 4-2 and leads the league in third-down conversion rate at 50.65 percent. Its defense has 21 sacks, tied for the league lead, while Tennessee has allowed only 11. Watch whether the Titans' line holds up against Dexter Lawrence II.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos chase a fourth straight win over Chiefs

stories.text: Broncos go for a fourth straight win and Payton's 200th
stories.summary: Denver is 5-2 and 3-0 at home when it hosts Kansas City on Sunday. Coach Sean Payton can reach his 200th career win in his 300th regular-season game. The Broncos also want a second AFC West win this season.

stories.text: Hufanga and Harvey out, Surtain has no game status
stories.summary: Safety Talanoa Hufanga and running back RJ Harvey are ruled out. Defensive lineman Zach Allen, tackle Garett Bolles, safety Brandon Jones and receiver Jaylen Waddle are questionable. Cornerback Pat Surtain II returned to full practice and has not been assigned a status after missing time since Week 4.

stories.text: Bo Nix ran for a 62-yard touchdown in the win over Arizona
stories.summary: Nix led Denver to 377 net yards and 30 points in the Week 7 win over the Cardinals, including a 62-yard touchdown run. Denver now goes for a fourth straight win.

stories.text: 21: sacks for the Broncos, tied for the NFL lead
stories.summary: Denver ties for the league lead with 21 sacks and ranks fifth in offensive line performance. The flip side: the Broncos allow 133 rushing yards a game, 28th in the league, and average 20.6 points.

stories.text: Chiefs at Empower Field, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver (5-2) hosts first-place Kansas City (5-1), which beat the Broncos in Week 1 and rushed for 220 yards. Watch whether Denver can slow Kenneth Walker and keep Patrick Mahomes under pressure.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs look to bounce back from Seattle in Denver

stories.text: Chiefs bounce back from a 20-3 loss in Seattle
stories.summary: Kansas City failed to reach the red zone against the Seahawks and went 3 for 11 on third down. Patrick Mahomes was pressured on 19 of 36 dropbacks. The Chiefs lead the AFC West by a half game and visit Denver on Sunday.

stories.text: Delane and Norman-Lott out, Mahomes and Kelce full
stories.summary: Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) are out. Defensive end Mason Thomas is questionable for a personal reason. Mahomes (knee), Travis Kelce (ankle), Nick Bolton, Creed Humphrey and Rashee Rice all practiced fully.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker leads the NFL at 116.8 rushing yards a game
stories.summary: Walker carries the league's top rushing average into Denver. He was held nearly 100 yards below that average against Seattle. A Chiefs ground game that gained 220 yards against the Broncos in Week 1 is the plan for Sunday.

stories.text: 39-8: Mahomes's record in AFC West games
stories.summary: A win Sunday would make Mahomes the fastest quarterback since the merger to reach 40 divisional wins, passing a mark shared by Tom Brady and Joe Montana. He is also 20-3 in divisional road games.

stories.text: At Denver, Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City (5-1) leads Denver (5-2) by a half game. A win gives the Chiefs the head-to-head tiebreaker and a two-game lead in the loss column. Watch the Broncos pass rush against Mahomes.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders seek to end four-game skid against Jets

stories.text: Raiders drop a fourth straight, 35-21 to the Rams
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed 28-6 at halftime and sits at 3-4 and 1-3 at home. Coach Klint Kubiak said the team must fix its red-zone play and third-quarter lapses on its own. The defense has allowed an average of 35.7 points during the slide.

stories.text: Patrick Johnson out, Powers-Johnson questionable
stories.summary: Edge Patrick Johnson (stinger) is out after three missed practices. Center Jackson Powers-Johnson (back) and receiver Jack Bech (forearm) are questionable. Brock Bowers (calf) practiced fully Thursday and Friday and carries no designation.

stories.text: Kirk Cousins threw for 295 yards in the loss to the Rams
stories.summary: Cousins went 26 of 44 with two touchdowns and no interceptions against Los Angeles. The Raiders still scored 26.1 points a game entering Week 8, seventh in the league, with the fourth-best passing offense.

stories.text: 74.7: rushing yards per game, 31st in the NFL
stories.summary: The Raiders run for 74.7 yards a game while allowing 143.6, 30th. The Rams held them to 48 yards on the ground last week. Ashton Jeanty needs 409 yards to pass Marcus Allen for second most by a Raider in his first two seasons.

stories.text: At Jets, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Las Vegas visits MetLife Stadium to face New York (2-5), which now starts former Raiders quarterback Geno Smith. The Jets list rookie edge David Bailey as doubtful with a groin injury. Las Vegas tries to end a four-game road skid.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers visit Rams after bye week

stories.text: Chargers are the last winless team in the NFL at 0-6
stories.summary: Los Angeles had a Week 7 bye and visits the Rams on Sunday. The offense ranks last in the league in expected points added per play, and the team has reportedly considered simplifying its playbook. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was hired Jan. 26.

stories.text: Derwin James among four Chargers ruled out
stories.summary: Safety Derwin James (hamstring), tackle Kayode Awosika (fibula), cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) and receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) are out. Cornerbacks Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley are questionable. Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris came off the report.

stories.text: Rookie center Jake Slaughter has started every game
stories.summary: Slaughter, a second-round pick, has started every game at center since starter Tyler Biadasz suffered a season-ending knee injury in August. He works beside an offensive line that starts four rookies and has been hit by injuries.

stories.text: -0.26: Chargers expected points added per play, last in the NFL
stories.summary: Next Gen Stats ranks Los Angeles last in EPA per play. In the 22-6 home loss to Kansas City, Justin Herbert went 22 of 37 for 204 yards with one interception and led the team with five carries for 26 yards.

stories.text: At Rams, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Chargers come off their bye to face Los Angeles at SoFi Stadium. Watch whether the rebuilt line can hold up against the Rams front, which held the Raiders to 48 rushing yards last week.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys eye NFC East after run-game romp

stories.text: Cowboys end skid and say the NFC East is in reach
stories.summary: Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 on Monday night to stop a two-game slide and move to 3-4. Dak Prescott said the division sits right in front of them if the wins keep coming. Coach Brian Schottenheimer called the win a return to the hunt, and ESPN Analytics gives Dallas a 57 percent shot at the title.

stories.text: Turpin and Winters out; Pickens questionable vs. Arizona
stories.summary: Receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf) are out. George Pickens (shoulder, hamstring) is questionable after a limited Friday, and tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) has missed two straight practices. Kenny Clark is also questionable, while Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke carry no designation.

stories.text: Javonte Williams runs for a career-high 155 yards
stories.summary: Williams carried 25 times for 155 yards and sealed the Eagles game with a 2-yard touchdown with 2:21 left. He averaged 6.2 yards a carry with a long of 34. He had averaged just 49 yards a game over the two prior contests.

stories.text: 204: rushing yards Dallas piled up on Philadelphia
stories.summary: The Cowboys ran for 204 yards and passed for 212 in the 38-21 win. They went 8 of 13 on third down and finished with 25 first downs. Prescott threw three touchdowns and no turnovers after two interceptions the week before.

stories.text: Cardinals visit AT&T Stadium at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas (3-4) hosts Arizona (2-5), which lost 30-16 to Denver last week and has dropped five of six. Watch whether the Cowboys keep feeding the run and whether Pickens suits up. Jerry Jones also signaled less urgency to trade picks before the deadline.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants hold first place heading into the bye

stories.text: Giants take bye alone atop the NFC East
stories.summary: The Giants beat Houston 27-21 in overtime and sit at 4-2-1 with sole possession of first place in the division for the first time since 2015. Devin Singletary scored the winner on a 30-yard run. They have 10 games left after the off week.

stories.text: Edmunds joins Dart and Burns on the season-ending list
stories.summary: Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds went on injured reserve with a shoulder injury, and quarterback Jaxson Dart and edge rusher Brian Burns are also out for the year. Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. left the Houston game with a hamstring injury. Jevon Holland and Greg Newsome II missed that game with concussions.

stories.text: Cam Skattebo breaks out for 124 yards on 17 carries
stories.summary: Skattebo set a career high with 124 rushing yards, scored from 16 yards and ripped a 42-yard run in overtime. Two weeks earlier against New Orleans he took six snaps and no carries. The Giants also got four catches for 83 yards from Malachi Fields.

stories.text: 56: tackles for rookie linebacker Arvell Reese
stories.summary: Reese leads the Giants with 56 tackles, along with 1.5 sacks and 5.5 tackles for loss. Through seven games he became the first Giants rookie to reach 50 tackles that fast since tackles became official in 1994. Micah McFadden added 10 tackles against Houston as he steps in for Edmunds.

stories.text: Giants are on bye in Week 8, then visit Philadelphia
stories.summary: New York has no game this week. In Week 9 the Giants go to Philadelphia, then host Washington on Thursday Night Football. Watch the kicking: Dominic Zvada missed from 44 and 56 yards against Houston, and Coach Harbaugh has no plan to replace him.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles hit Washington on a five-game skid

stories.text: Eagles turn to McKee with Hurts out for the year
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts has blood clots in his lungs and is unlikely to return before 2027, which leaves Tanner McKee running the offense. McKee, a sixth-round pick in 2023, is 1-2 as a starter with 812 yards, six touchdowns and one interception over his first three starts. Philadelphia lost to Dallas on Monday night.

stories.text: Smith, Wicks, Jones and Campbell out at Washington
stories.summary: The Eagles ruled out receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring, quad) and returner Britain Covey (knee). Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) practiced in a limited way Friday and is set to play. No one carries a questionable tag.

stories.text: Barkley keeps producing while banged up
stories.summary: Barkley averages 5.7 yards a carry, second in the league behind Kenneth Walker's 5.8. He gained 72 total yards and scored on nine touches against Dallas. He is working through hamstring and back problems, so his workload bears watching.

stories.text: 32nd: Eagles rank last in yards per play
stories.summary: Philadelphia is 29th in points per game and 32nd in yards per play. Washington's defense is 31st in points allowed and 22nd in yards per play allowed. Something gives on Sunday night.

stories.text: Eagles visit Commanders on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Kickoff is 8:20 p.m. ET Sunday on NBC at Northwest Stadium. The Eagles beat Washington 24-22 in Week 1 and are trying to end a five-game losing streak. Watch McKee against a defense that blitzes 43.9 percent of the time, second most in the league.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders lose Payne for the season

stories.text: Commanders lose Daron Payne to a foot fracture
stories.summary: Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in Friday's practice, per a report from ESPN's Adam Schefter. The 2018 first-round pick had one sack, 14 tackles and five quarterback hits this year. His injury also ends any trade talk before the deadline.

stories.text: Kinlaw likely out; four Commanders miss practice
stories.summary: Center Nick Allegretti (back), tight end John Bates (shoulder), receiver Treylon Burks (foot) and tackle Javon Kinlaw (knee) did not practice, and Dan Quinn said Kinlaw will likely not play. Charles Omenihu and Jer'Zhan Newton were limited. Quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow) practiced fully.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels is back and producing
stories.summary: Daniels threw for 199 yards, ran for 103 and scored twice on the ground in the 27-27 tie with the Giants. He followed with 300 passing yards against San Francisco. He returned from an elbow dislocation but has not won a start since Week 5 of 2025.

stories.text: 81.8%: the red zone touchdown rate Washington allows
stories.summary: Washington's defense gives up touchdowns on 81.8 percent of red zone trips, worst in the league. Philadelphia's offense ranks fourth, scoring on 14 of 19 trips. The Commanders have also lost six straight primetime games.

stories.text: Eagles come to Northwest Stadium for Sunday night
stories.summary: Washington (1-4-1) hosts Philadelphia at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC after its bye. The Commanders are on a three-game home winless streak, and Terry McLaurin is out for the year, so Stefon Diggs is the top target. Daniels has not lost a game when the defense allows 22 or fewer points.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears bring healthy Williams to Seattle

stories.text: Bears take a healthy Caleb Williams to Seattle at 5-2
stories.summary: Chicago beat New England 30-24 on Thursday night to reach 5-2, its fourth win in five games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in his second game back from a hamstring injury that cost him three starts. The Bears now close the week on Monday night at Seattle.

stories.text: Bears list four questionable and one doubtful for Seattle
stories.summary: Linebacker Anthony Johnson Jr. is doubtful. Running back Kyle Monangai, linebackers Jack Sanborn and T.J. Edwards and cornerback Malik Muhammad II are questionable. Tight end Cole Kmet, who left the New England game on a cart with a knee injury, is on injured reserve along with Braxton Jones and Coby Bryant.

stories.text: Luther Burden III is becoming Chicago's top deep threat
stories.summary: Burden caught four passes for 130 yards and a touchdown against the Patriots, all of it in the first half. He has 491 receiving yards this season, and 225 of them came in the last two games. A 58-yard grab in the first quarter set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown.

stories.text: 10: takeaways for a Bears defense that still gives up yards
stories.summary: Chicago has forced 10 turnovers and ranks fourth in pressure rate with 19 sacks. The same unit allows the most yards per play in the league. Seattle's Sam Darnold has thrown eight interceptions, four of them under pressure.

stories.text: Bears at Seahawks, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Chicago (5-2) visits Lumen Field in Seattle (4-3) on Monday, Nov. 2. Watch whether the Bears pass rush can get to Darnold and whether Monangai and the linebackers return.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions host unbeaten Vikings

stories.text: Lions host unbeaten Vikings on a two-game win streak
stories.summary: Detroit beat Green Bay 20-17 on a Jake Bates 22-yard field goal as time expired. The Lions are 4-2 with two straight wins and sit third in the NFC North behind Minnesota and Chicago. Sunday gives them a shot at the last unbeaten team in the league.

stories.text: Kerby Joseph is out; Gibbs and St. Brown practice in full
stories.summary: Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) is ruled out. Cornerback Roger McCreary (foot) is questionable. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs (shoulder) and receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) sat out Wednesday but were full participants Thursday and Friday.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs carries the load with David Montgomery gone
stories.summary: Gibbs is averaging career highs of 22.3 carries and 103.3 rushing yards per game, plus 5.3 catches. He has 552 yards and nine touchdowns in six career games against Minnesota. He sat out Wednesday practice with a shoulder issue and returned to full work Thursday.

stories.text: 112.5: Jared Goff's passer rating, best in the NFL
stories.summary: Goff has 14 touchdown passes and no interceptions, and his rating against the blitz is 123.3, third in the league. Minnesota coordinator Brian Flores brings pressure often and sacked Goff 10 times in two games last season. Goff has beaten Flores-coached teams four times before.

stories.text: Vikings at Lions, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Detroit (4-2) hosts Minnesota (6-0) at Ford Field on Sunday, Nov. 1. Watch Goff against the Vikings blitz and how safety Brian Branch, back from an Achilles tear, holds up in his second game. Kerby Joseph's absence leaves the secondary thin.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers top Panthers, head to New England

stories.text: Packers hold off Panthers 27-19 to reach 5-3
stories.summary: Green Bay won Thursday night at Lambeau Field and improved to 5-3 after a loss at Detroit the week before. The Packers led 27-10 in the third quarter and then let Carolina close within eight. They outgained the Panthers 354 yards to 258 despite three turnovers.

stories.text: Watson cleared to return after chest scare against Carolina
stories.summary: Receiver Christian Watson left in an ambulance with a chest injury after a 53-yard catch, was cleared at a hospital and came back to finish with 8 catches for 113 yards. ESPN reports a broken rib. Tight end Josh Whyle was checked for a concussion in the first half.

stories.text: Jordan Love throws three touchdowns in 30-of-41 night
stories.summary: Love finished with 288 yards, three touchdown passes and one interception for a 106.6 rating. His scoring throws went to Tucker Kraft, Matthew Golden and Josh Jacobs. Jacobs crossed 10,000 career total yards on his touchdown catch.

stories.text: 6: sacks of Bryce Young by the Green Bay defense
stories.summary: Young went down six times and took nine hits while the Packers held Carolina to 258 total yards. The Panthers still outgained Green Bay 109 yards to 32 in the fourth quarter. Brenton Cox Jr. recorded his first sack of the season.

stories.text: Packers at Patriots, Sunday, Nov. 8, 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Green Bay played Thursday, so it has no game this Sunday. The next one is at Gillette Stadium against New England. The extra days help Watson and Whyle recover.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings visit Detroit

stories.text: Unbeaten Vikings win again, but the offense still lags
stories.summary: Minnesota is 6-0 for the first time since 2009 after a 16-10 win over Indianapolis. The offense ranks 23rd in scoring and converted 3 of 11 third downs. Kyler Murray went 14 of 24 for 150 yards, and coach Kevin O'Connell said the team needs more points.

stories.text: Vikings clear Jones, Huber and O'Neill for Detroit
stories.summary: Running back Aaron Jones (knee), guard Joe Huber (knee) and tackle Brian O'Neill (knee) all practiced fully Friday with no game designation. Safety Jay Ward (knee) is questionable. Tackle Christian Darrisaw and safety Harrison Smith have rest days listed.

stories.text: Justin Jefferson owns Ford Field in his 100th game
stories.summary: Jefferson has 52 catches for 831 yards and three touchdowns in six games in Detroit, the most receiving yards by a visiting player there. Sunday is his 100th career game, and his 8,782 yards rank third through 100 games behind Julio Jones and Lance Alworth. His yards per game since the start of 2025 sit at 61.4, well below his first five seasons.

stories.text: 85%: Vikings sent four or more rushers on Colts' dropbacks
stories.summary: Brian Flores called blitzes on 85 percent of Indianapolis pass plays, the highest rate by any team in a game since tracking began in 2016. Minnesota leads the league in interceptions and in sacks per pass attempt. The Vikings have drawn only six penalties for 70 yards in six games.

stories.text: Vikings at Lions, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Minnesota (6-0) visits Detroit (4-2) at Ford Field on Sunday, Nov. 1. Minnesota wears purple, which it has never done against the Lions. Watch their top scoring defense against Detroit's offense, the league's second best.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons ride 49ers upset into Tampa

stories.text: Falcons end San Francisco's unbeaten start with a 29-20 win
stories.summary: Atlanta beat the previously unbeaten 49ers in Week 7 and forced four takeaways to do it. The offense has averaged 31.0 points over its last five games. The win leaves the Falcons at 3-4 in a wide-open NFC South.

stories.text: Brian Robinson is out, Cameron Williams could return at tackle
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) is out at Tampa Bay. Tackle Cameron Williams, coming off injured reserve with an ankle injury, is questionable, along with cornerback Billy Bowman Jr., linebacker Divine Deablo and corner Avieon Terrell (illness). Defensive end Samson Ebukam and receivers Beaux Collins and Olamide Zaccheaus carry the same designation.

stories.text: Michael Penix Jr. found his rhythm against the 49ers
stories.summary: Penix threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions against San Francisco, and Tampa Bay's game notes say he was not sacked on 34 dropbacks. Over his last five starts he has nine touchdowns and one interception. He returned this season from a torn ACL.

stories.text: 907: Bijan Robinson leads the NFL in scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Robinson has 907 yards from scrimmage through Week 7 and averages 5.4 yards per carry. He ran for 704 yards and five touchdowns on the ground. He had 122 scrimmage yards against San Francisco without scoring.

stories.text: Falcons visit Tampa Bay today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Atlanta plays at Raymond James Stadium in a divisional game. The Falcons' fourth-ranked rushing offense meets a Bucs defense that ranks second against the run. Watch Kyle Pitts, who has four touchdowns in Atlanta's last three games.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers fire DC Evero after Green Bay loss

stories.text: Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero
stories.summary: Carolina dismissed Evero and pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley the morning after a 27-19 loss at Green Bay that dropped the team to 3-4. Defensive line coach Todd Wash takes over and will call plays. Evero's defenses never ranked higher than 15th in points allowed in four seasons.

stories.text: Jaelan Phillips' hamstring kept him out at Green Bay
stories.summary: The edge rusher missed a second straight game with a recurring hamstring injury that began in Week 4. Left guard Damien Lewis (knee) and cornerback Akayleb Evans were also out Thursday. The extra days before Denver give all three time to heal, though no new status has been reported.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard did his work at Lambeau
stories.summary: Hubbard carried 22 times for 81 yards and a touchdown and added seven catches for 38 yards. Bryce Young went 23 of 41 for 209 yards with one touchdown and one interception, and Green Bay sacked him six times. Jalen Coker caught a 26-yard touchdown on fourth-and-3 late.

stories.text: 153.2: Panthers' run defense was the league's worst
stories.summary: Carolina allowed 153.2 rushing yards per game entering Thursday, the most in the NFL. Under Evero the defense allowed 200 or more rushing yards 12 times, also the league high in that span. At Green Bay it held the Packers to 66 rushing yards.

stories.text: Panthers are off this week, then host Denver on Nov. 8
stories.summary: Carolina has no game in Week 8 and does not play again until the Nov. 8 home game against the Broncos. That gives Wash a full extra week to install his version of the defense. Kickoff time and network were not confirmed in the sources checked.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints use bye to fix a dead run game

stories.text: Moore calls Saints' bye a chance to self-scout the run game
stories.summary: New Orleans lost 16-10 to Pittsburgh in Paris and is 2-5 heading into its bye. Coach Kellen Moore said the staff will dig into why the ground game collapsed but would not promise major changes. He pointed to the six division games left as the path to winning the NFC South.

stories.text: Travis Etienne could return from IR; Jordyn Tyson still rehabbing
stories.summary: Running back Travis Etienne is on injured reserve and eligible to return against Cleveland in Week 9, though Moore said a medical evaluation will decide it. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson is moving well in rehab, and the bye should clarify his status.

stories.text: Tyler Shough threw 278 yards but made one costly mistake
stories.summary: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards against Pittsburgh. His only interception came in the red zone on the second half's opening drive, a pass for Chris Olave that linebacker Payton Wilson picked off at the 10. It was his first red-zone interception of the season.

stories.text: 18: rushing yards on 17 carries in the Paris loss
stories.summary: The Saints ran for 18 yards on 17 attempts, their lowest rushing total since 1999. A week earlier they ran for a season-high 175 yards against the Giants. Only 3 of their 19 first downs came on the ground.

stories.text: Saints are on bye, then host Cleveland on Nov. 8
stories.summary: New Orleans is off this week. Its next game is Sunday, Nov. 8 against the Browns at the Superdome, noon Central (1 p.m. ET) on CBS. Moore plans a light Monday of practice and weight work, then a full week of Cleveland prep.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs chase first home win against Falcons

stories.text: Bucs seek first home win after 43-13 rout at Carolina
stories.summary: Tampa Bay won its first division game of the season in Charlotte and now hosts Atlanta without a home win in 2026. The Bucs lost to Cleveland, Minnesota and Carolina at home before a Pittsburgh overtime loss after leading 16-3 in the fourth quarter. They are 2-5.

stories.text: Emeka Egbuka out, Gainwell and Goedeke questionable
stories.summary: Receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) is ruled out and leads the team with 28 catches. Running back Kenneth Gainwell (hip) and tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) are questionable. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb), safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) and linebacker Josiah Trotter (illness) carry no designation.

stories.text: Yaya Diaby piled up three sacks at Carolina
stories.summary: Diaby's three sacks were the first by a Bucs defender in a game since Devin White in 2020. He has 16 quarterback pressures, tied for the team lead. He battled an illness during the week but was upgraded to full practice.

stories.text: 258: rushing yards for Tampa Bay at Carolina
stories.summary: The Bucs ran for 258 yards, the fourth most in a game in franchise history. Baker Mayfield threw only 11 passes, the fewest in a Tampa Bay win since the 1970s. The ground game ranks third in the NFL while the passing offense ranks last.

stories.text: Bucs host Atlanta today at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay and Atlanta meet at Raymond James Stadium. The Bucs have the league's second-ranked run defense, and Atlanta has won four of the last five in the series. Watch whether Mayfield throws more downfield in his second game back from a thumb dislocation.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Love returns as Cardinals chase Dallas again

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love cleared to return as Arizona tries to stop a skid at Dallas
stories.summary: The Cardinals sit at 2-5 after a 30-16 loss to Denver last Sunday. Coach Mike LaFleur confirmed that rookie running back Jeremiyah Love will play against the Cowboys after missing two games with an ankle injury. Arizona has won four straight against Dallas.

stories.text: Nolen and Gaines out, three Cardinals questionable at Dallas
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Walter Nolen (ankle) and lineman Jon Gaines II (ankle) are out. Lineman Hjalte Froholdt (knee), cornerback Max Melton (knee) and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) are questionable. Receiver Michael Wilson (sore ribs) will play, LaFleur said.

stories.text: Trey McBride leads the NFL with 59 catches
stories.summary: McBride caught 10 passes for 111 yards against Denver. Pro Football Focus has charged him with no drops on 74 targets this season. He gives Arizona its steadiest offensive weapon during a losing stretch.

stories.text: 145.7: rushing yards per game Dallas allows
stories.summary: The Cowboys give up 145.7 rushing yards a game and rank 29th in rush EPA allowed. That is the opening Love walks into on Sunday. He has 245 yards on 67 carries this season, a 3.7 average.

stories.text: Cardinals at Cowboys, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona visits AT&T Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1, with Kenny Albert and Greg Olsen on the FOX call. Dallas is coming off a 38-21 win at Philadelphia. Watch whether Arizona can run the ball against the league's weakest rush defense.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams chase a first winning streak against winless LAC

stories.text: Rams look for their first winning streak of 2026 against the Chargers
stories.summary: Los Angeles is 3-4 and bounced back at Las Vegas after two straight home losses, both decided on final-play field goal attempts. The Rams stood pat at the trade deadline and are counting on injured players to return. They host a Chargers team that is 0-6.

stories.text: McDuffie, Parkinson and Shelton questionable vs. Chargers
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie (groin), tight end Colby Parkinson (rib), lineman Coleman Shelton (hip) and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) are questionable. Long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) is doubtful. Linebacker Nate Landman (concussion) carries no designation.

stories.text: Matthew Stafford hit 79% of his throws at Las Vegas
stories.summary: Stafford completed 79 percent of his passes last Sunday, his best mark as a Ram. He has topped 70 percent in three straight games. His average air yards per attempt fell under five in each of the last two games, a sign of how short and efficient the offense has become.

stories.text: 15: Chargers giveaways, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Los Angeles' other team has turned the ball over 15 times, and Justin Herbert has thrown an interception in every game. Herbert has also been hit on 20.4 percent of his dropbacks, the highest rate in the league. The Rams defense has 10 sacks and six takeaways, so this is a chance to add to both.

stories.text: Chargers at SoFi Stadium, Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Rams (3-4) host the Chargers (0-6) on Sunday, Nov. 1. Kickoff is 1:05 p.m. PT. Watch the Chargers' blitz, which generates a 52.5 percent pressure rate, against Rams backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum in pass protection.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers bye at 6-1 with reinforcements coming

stories.text: 49ers hold a two-game NFC West lead going into the bye
stories.summary: San Francisco is 6-1, and its lone loss came to Atlanta, 29-20, when it turned the ball over four times. The team has the week off and plans to use it to clean up turnovers, penalties and kicking. A number of injured players could return for the next game.

stories.text: Bosa, Evans and Samuel eye Week 9 returns after the bye
stories.summary: Defensive end Nick Bosa (calf), receiver Mike Evans and receiver Deebo Samuel are all targeting the Raiders game. Evans needs no more testing, according to Kyle Shanahan. Samuel's return is expected but not promised. Sources differ on his injury: one lists a hamstring, another a quad.

stories.text: Renardo Green ties for the NFL lead with three interceptions
stories.summary: The cornerback has allowed a 55.1 passer rating in coverage, 17th lowest among 195 qualified defensive backs. He is one of the best performers on a team that sits atop the division at the bye.

stories.text: 26.7%: the lowest pressure rate allowed in the NFL
stories.summary: The 49ers offensive line has given up pressure on 26.7 percent of dropbacks, the league's best mark. Brock Purdy has been sacked seven times and pressured 62 times on 232 dropbacks. The line has also opened lanes for Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black.

stories.text: Bye this week, then Raiders on Nov. 8 at 4:25 p.m. ET
stories.summary: San Francisco does not play in Week 8. The Niners host the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi's Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 8, at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The target is to have the injured veterans back for that one.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Charbonnet returns as Seahawks host Bears Monday

stories.text: Zach Charbonnet makes his 2026 debut on Monday night
stories.summary: The running back tore his ACL in last season's divisional round and will play against Chicago with no game designation. Guard Quenton Nelson, acquired from the Colts, is set for his Seahawks debut. Josh Jones starts at left tackle.

stories.text: Cross, Shaheed and Jones out; Nwosu doubtful vs. Bears
stories.summary: Left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) are out. Outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) is doubtful. Linebackers Drake Thomas and Chazz Surratt are back, and Thomas returns to the starting lineup.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba wins Air & Ground honors again
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught for 150 yards and a touchdown against Kansas City in Week 7. It was his sixth 100-yard game of the season and his second Air & Ground Player of the Week award.

stories.text: 1st: Seattle's defense in opponent yards per play
stories.summary: Seattle leads the league in opponent yards per play, according to a Week 8 breakdown. Chicago's defense allows the most yards per play, mostly against the run. Seattle's offense ranks 24th in EPA per play and averages 3.9 yards per carry, which is where Charbonnet comes in.

stories.text: Bears at Lumen Field, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Seattle (4-3) hosts Chicago (5-2) on Monday, Nov. 2. Watch how the Seahawks protect Sam Darnold with Cross out, and whether Chicago's pass rush gets home.
